You will edit a spreadsheet to calculate the skirting boards needed for a room.
Enter, right aligned in the footer, the text Spreadsheet by followed by a space then your name,
Save this as a spreadsheet with the filename Skirting_ followed by your
Merge cells A1 to D1, A3 to B3, A7 to B7, C7 to D7, A11 to B11, F2 to G2 and H2 to H3.
Format the spreadsheet to look like this:
A B C D E F G H
Centre align the empty cells in the ranges B8:D9 and C11:C20.
Skirting boards can only be bought in certain lengths. These are called stock lengths. Cells H4 to H13
show the stock lengths available. When fitting skirting boards, you buy a bigger length than needed
and cut it down. The maximum stock length available is 3.6 metres.
Re-uploading, mirroring or re-hosting this file on any other website or domain is unauthorised and traceable.

Examine cells F3 to H13. Columns F and G show the length of skirting board needed and column H
shows the corresponding stock length you buy. For example:
• for lengths less than (<) 1.2 metres, you would buy a 1.2 metre stock length
• for lengths greater than or equal to (>=) 1.2 metres and less than (<) 1.5 metres, you would buy a
13 Create a named range with the name Slength for cells F4 to H13.
Place a screenshot of this named range in your Evidence Document showing the name and
If a wall is less than or equal to 3.6 metres long, a single board can be used. If a wall is greater than
3.6 metres long, two skirting boards are needed. No wall will be greater than 7.2 metres long.
14 Enter in cell B8 a formula to divide the length of the room by the longest Skirting length (metres)
in column F. Edit this formula so that the results are rounded up to the nearest whole number. [2]
15 Enter in cell B9 a formula to divide the width of the room by the longest Skirting length (metres) in
column F. Edit this formula so that the results are rounded up to the nearest whole number. [1]
16 Enter in cell D8 a formula that displays the value held in cell H13 if more than one board is
needed for the length. If only one board is needed for the length, the formula must display a
Enter in cell D9 a formula that displays the value held in cell H13 if more than one board is
needed for the width. If only one board is needed for the width, the formula must display a value
17 Enter in cell C8 a formula to subtract the contents of cell D8 from the length of the room.
Enter in cell C9 a formula to subtract the contents of cell D9 from the width of the room.
Edit both of these formulas to look up and display the stock length needed. You must use the
named range Slength in your formulas.
